population.note: FICTIONAL. Of ~275M adults, 27.7% current ≈ 76.2M and 40.5% ever ≈ 111.4M. That leaves 12.8% (≈35.2M) who have used and are off now, and ≈164M who have never used. Cycling: ever 40.5 − current 27.7 = 12.8 pts off now. About 14.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈4.5 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (14.5+4.5)/40.5 ≈ 47%. Ever-use rose 5.0 pts (limit 5.7) and current rose 2.7. This fits the parent's ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart rate. Employer retreat pushed millions off. Generic semaglutide at $35–69 cash brought most of them back within a year, often on a cheaper molecule than before. Age check: 18–29 18.2% × 52M ≈ 9.5M; 30–49 31.5% × 91M ≈ 28.7M; 50–64 40% × 62M ≈ 24.8M; 65+ 19% × 70M ≈ 13.3M; total ≈ 76.3M ≈ 27.7%. The fastest growth is under 50. The new users are low-dose 'metabolic health' and longevity users without obesity, and young cash generic users. The 65+ band rose only 2 pts. Three things held it down: the bone data, the Novo fracture-memo disclosure (2033) and DEXA pauses. Roughly one in four 65+ ever-users is now off on medical advice. Income: generics lifted the bottom third (21→25) more than employer retreat cut the middle (26→27, net of cash switchers). The top third (28→31) grew through longevity regimens. Off-drug populations: ≈35M lapsed users, many in regain after losing employer coverage; ≈2.2M on imported tirzepatide or retatrutide copies; and never-users, now concentrated among rural over-60s, people with contraindications, and a visible under-30 'unmedicated' cohort. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, mostly 12+, with a cash generic tail that is not tracked. The full adolescent bone dataset went to FDA in 2034 and is under review. Nearly two in five children now live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The Part D obesity benefit (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity) and the CMS continuation standard are unchanged. Part D plans moved obesity users onto generic semaglutide after the Feb 2033 entry. The plan net for generic is ≈$45/month with a $10 generic-tier copay. Brands stay at the $199 negotiated rate with the $50 copay. Medicare pays 18.4% of fills ≈ 14.0M users: ≈6.4M diabetes and ≈7.6M obesity, of whom ~55% are on generic by end-2034. Obesity-benefit gross: average (0.55×$45 + 0.45×$199) ≈ $114 × 7.6M × 12 ≈ $10.4B. Beneficiaries pay (3.42M × $50 + 4.18M × $10) × 12 ≈ $2.55B. Program net ≈ $7.9B, down from ≈$12.2B in 2032. The old CBO score of ≈$190B over ten years is now an overstatement, and CBO has not re-scored it. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC hold the 90% match. Medicaid pays 14.2% of fills ≈ 10.8M users. At ~70% generic at $40 and 30% brand at $199, the average is ≈$88, so 10.8M × $88 × 12 ≈ $11.4B gross, against ≈$24.4B in 2032.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month and generic tirzepatide filings abroad. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, plus API for most of the remaining gray trade. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt: generic semaglutide is standard. In the US, generic injectable semaglutide has been on the market since Feb 2033 (seven ANDA holders by end-2034). Oral semaglutide and tirzepatide remain branded.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse. Under the Sep 2031 settlements, generic injectable semaglutide launched in Feb 2033. Seven makers were selling by end-2034, at $35–69/month cash at chain pharmacies and discount platforms. Section 232 pharma tariffs largely exempt generics. Brands followed only partly. Tirzepatide is $179 on the federal portal, orforglipron high-dose $129, retatrutide 12 mg $399 direct ($1,499 list), amycretin $349 direct and survodutide $329 direct. Payer mix of ≈76.2M users: commercial 28.9% (22.0M, now mostly diabetes, cardiovascular, OSA, CKD and MASH codes), Medicare 18.4% (14.0M), Medicaid 14.2% (10.8M), cash/direct 35.7% (27.2M) and imported/counterfeit 2.9% (2.2M); the sum is 76.2M. Cash includes ≈10M obesity users dropped by employers who now buy generic, ≈5.8M low-dose longevity or 'metabolic health' users without obesity, ≈2.4M 'calm/focus' subscribers (down from 3.5M) and ≈1.0M compulsion users on and off label. Imports collapsed to tirzepatide and retatrutide copies. Of employers still covering weight management, ~80% gate it. US incretin market ≈$99B (commercial 22.0M × $150 × 12 ≈ $39.6B; Medicare diabetes 6.4M × $130 × 12 ≈ $10.0B; Medicare obesity ≈$10.4B; Medicaid ≈$11.4B; cash 27.2M × ≈$85 × 12 ≈ $27.7B), against ≈$145B in 2032, with ex-US ≈$22B.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; US generics since Feb 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Mar 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus; gambling-disorder indication Apr 2034)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. high-dose maintenance form approved Mar 2034)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing of generic semaglutide in adults without obesity (≈5.8M), sold by gym chains, concierge practices and telehealth
compulsive shopping, screen and sexual compulsion (off-label extension of the gambling indication)
'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (≈2.4M, shrinking since the label change)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial still enrolling)
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is met by an existing product in a new form. In Mar 2034 FDA approved a high-dose maintenance form of orforglipron (Foundayo) after a 72-week head-to-head trial: 15.9% loss, against 16.3% for injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg, which met noninferiority. It does not match tirzepatide or retatrutide. Survodutide was approved for chronic weight management in Mar 2033 with DEXA in its label. MariTide received a complete response letter in Jul 2033 asking for 104-week BMD data, and resubmission is expected in 2035. Novo sought a new indication for oral semaglutide to keep branded exclusivity once injectable generics arrived. It filed in Mar 2033 for gambling disorder and was approved in Apr 2034 on two phase-3 trials. The label puts reduced reward responsiveness in its warnings. Bimagrumab combinations have read out in phase 3 but are not filed, and Lilly guides to a 2035 filing. Lean-mass and bone-sparing agents remain the biggest gap in the pipeline. No oral triple agonist is beyond phase 2.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and leading cause of stops. Generic switching produced a wave of re-titration GI episodes in 2033.
Rising in absolute numbers with high-dose triples and survodutide.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Imported copies still confound reports, though less than before.
Medicare claims estimate ≈1.7M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria. Lean mass is ~30–40% of weight lost in untrained users over 50.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring required in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and survodutide labels; CMS annual DEXA for long-term 65+ unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈7.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. At ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture risk × 0.35 excess, that is ≈14,700 excess hip fractures a year against ~300,000 US total, plus a vertebral fracture excess in cycling postmenopausal women aged 50–64. DEXA waits have eased to 8–14 weeks as mobile capacity has grown. Unsealed Novo documents show an internal 2029 pooled analysis with a fracture HR of ~1.4 in women aged 55+ that was not submitted to FDA.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class-wide fracture language strengthened in Warnings and Precautions (2034). FDA ordered sponsors to reanalyse bone data. DOJ–Novo civil settlement (Sep 2033). The CMS bone-pause code is unchanged, and private plans are still not bound by it.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Uncommon at standard and low doses; ~12% of 12 mg retatrutide users versus ~5% of comparators cross the SHAPS threshold. The gambling-disorder trials found it in ~4% of treated participants versus ~1% on placebo. No independent study of low-dose 'calm' users yet, though one funded by NIH is enrolling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Since Apr 2034 it is labelled as an uncommon adverse reaction across the class, with dose-dependence noted. It is in the warnings of the gambling-disorder label. FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Large in absolute terms because of employer drop-offs in 2033–34. Most restart within a year on cash generic.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code for Medicare only; the Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users and now also seen in low-dose longevity users who skip meals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance and the Part D counselling screen; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The full adolescent dataset (2034) confirms lower BMD accrual in a subset of rapid losers. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA review of the adolescent data is ongoing; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imports are down to ≈2.2M users, mostly on tirzepatide and retatrutide copies. Poison-centre calls about counterfeits fell ~40%. Dosing errors from generic pen-device differences are a new, small category.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts continue; 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand; Safe Pens bill still stalled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use, even after sarcopenia adjustment.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Mandatory fall screening in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Worse in the 2033 cohort that lost employer coverage. DEXA cohorts show the same weight with less lean mass and more visceral fat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide and with survodutide.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean-mass and bone loss in normal-weight long-term low-dose users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Small DEXA cohorts from longevity clinics show measurable lean-mass decline in non-obese users with no metabolic benefit beyond baseline. The sample is small and the users are self-selected.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; off-label. Endocrine societies issued a statement against routine use without obesity.

food_and_beverage.state: Salty-snack volume falls ~3% a year and confectionery ~4%. Protein and 'bone-forward' dairy keep growing. A new 'appetite' segment of full-fat, unapologetically indulgent premium lines sells in Brooklyn, Austin and LA to young unmedicated buyers and to off-dose weekenders. Creatine-fortified products are moving into the mainstream grocery aisle.

alcohol.state: Seventh year of spirits volume decline. The decline has slowed because employer-dropped users who cycle off drink again for a few months. Craft and natural wine do well with the 'unmedicated vitality' crowd. Sportsbooks report lower handle per active account in high-uptake states.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover is flat to slightly down. Half-portions are standard. In Brooklyn, Austin and Atlanta, 'appetite rooms' with large-plate tasting menus and steak-and-potatoes revivals are the hardest reservations for diners under 35. Chains run 'full table' weekends.

apparel.state: Size churn from employer drop-offs lasted through 2033. Growth has moved to athletic cuts with more shoulder and thigh room, made for lifters. Mid-market brands rebuild their size curves around muscle, and the 'generic thin' sample-size look is discounted.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains and mobile scanners keep expanding. Gym chains sell 'metabolic memberships' that bundle a generic semaglutide microdose prescription with strength training. Lean-mass index has become a marketing metric. The shortage of trainers qualified for older lifters persists.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management fell from 66% to 41% as employers pointed to $49 generics and to the bone liabilities. Coverage now concentrates on diabetes, CV, OSA, CKD and MASH codes. Of the plans that still cover, ~80% gate. Pharmacy trend has turned negative for incretins. Fall and fracture costs keep landing on Medicare Parts A and C.

pharma.state: Volume is up and revenue down: the US incretin market is ≈$99B, against ≈$145B in 2032. Novo is hit hardest by generic entry and by the fracture-memo settlement, and is leaning on oral semaglutide's gambling indication. Lilly keeps share through tirzepatide, retatrutide and high-dose Foundayo. Indian generic makers are major US suppliers. Bone-agent and DEXA makers are still growing.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer signals discipline or money because a $39 pen buys it. Among under-40s in high-income metros the scarce body is 'dense': visible muscle, good DEXA numbers, and an appetite you can show at dinner. 'Generic thin' (slim, soft-armed, slightly stooped) is a mild slur aimed at cash-generic users. Over 60, trained shoulders still mark a well-run regimen.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is nearly equal across income (25% bottom, 31% top), but bodies are diverging. The top third runs retatrutide or amycretin with coaching, scheduled DEXA, antiresorptives and creatine, or opts out and displays 'unmedicated vitality'. The middle third lost employer coverage and moved to cash generic semaglutide with no scans. In Dayton and Phoenix the DEXA van queue is still a social space. In Austin, people screenshot lean-mass index at the gym.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals remain the weekday norm. Under-35s in Brooklyn and Austin hold 'appetite dinners' where seconds are expected and dosing down for the weekend is part of the plan. Church potlucks and Sunday full-table dinners continue unchanged in Memphis and Tulsa.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps keep the on/off/pausing field and some now offer an optional lean-mass badge. 'Unmedicated' has moved from a niche filter to an aspirational one among under-30s. Advice columns field complaints about partners who 'got thin on generics and stopped eating with me'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is being revalued. For older and insured users it is still a symptom to manage. For young urban cohorts a visible, healthy hunger signals vitality and means you are not dependent. The old backlash coalition has merged into this mood without leading it, and influencers who once sold berberine now sell 'hunger training'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The Apr 2034 class label lists reduced reward responsiveness as an uncommon adverse reaction that rises with dose. At ~12% vs ~5% on 12 mg retatrutide, and with ~7M people on top-dose triple or dual regimens, that implies ~450–500k excess cases. Low-dose users (≈2.4M calm subscribers, ≈5.8M longevity microdosers) are unmeasured. An NIH cohort is enrolling.
interior_life.framing: Side effect in the label and treatment in the gambling indication: one mechanism under two names. Clinicians now say 'reward modulation' only when the patient has a compulsion. The 'calm' brands still sell 'calm' under FTC orders, but the label language travels with the product.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the label change, the major HR benefits platform removed 'focus' subscriptions from its standard lifestyle catalogue in mid-2034. They are now available only as 'clinician-prescribed'. Fleets and warehouses still prefer continuous use. Sales and creative staff keep dosing down before pitches. EAPs now refer employees with gambling problems to the oral indication.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' has become a mainstream selling point among young musicians and comedians in Nashville and Austin, part of the vitality aesthetic. Critics call the 2031–33 records the 'grey era'. Sportsbook and loot-box operators watch the gambling indication closely.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose as a matter of routine. With the label in place, people say 'the grey' in clinics more freely and with less shrugging. Some couples now negotiate dose-down weekends as explicitly as contraception.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Senate hearings on the Novo memo framed the drug as a corporate-candour story rather than a safety one. Gambling-industry lobbyists and addiction advocates disagree over whether sportsbooks should fund treatment. The continuation-standard fight continues but has cooled as generics cut the stakes. 'Calm voter' claims remain unpublished.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and now openly punitive about disclosure. It strengthened class fracture language, ordered bone-data reanalyses, issued a CRL to MariTide over BMD, and approved the gambling indication with reward-blunting warnings. It approved seven generic semaglutide ANDAs. Import enforcement stays selective. FTC orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new state action. The permanent Part D obesity benefit and the 90% Medicaid match in 31 states plus DC continue on unchanged statutory terms. Generic substitution by plans has cut program net spending without any new law.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weigh-ins, ≥5% loss at 6 months or a clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and the 90-day bone pause. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Private gating continues in the shrinking set of employer plans that still cover, and BMI-linked wellness surcharges persist. Cash generic users are outside all of these regimes.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide. Fleets require DEXA for drivers over 55. Military accession policy is unchanged; the Air Force allows waivers after 12 months stable.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian finished-dose makers are now the main US generic semaglutide suppliers, and the US–India framework is invoked to keep generics tariff-exempt. Chinese API remains upstream. The Section 232 tariffs remain on branded products. Lilly's retatrutide allocation ended in mid-2033.

events.event: Generic injectable semaglutide launches in the US under the 2031 settlements. Seven makers are shipping by year-end, and chain-pharmacy cash prices fall to $35–69 a month

An annual employer benefits survey finds one in three large employers has dropped weight-management coverage since January and now covers incretins only under diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea and kidney codes, citing $49 generics and bone liabilities

Novo Nordisk settles the DOJ civil case for $2.4 billion. Unsealed documents show a 2029 internal analysis with a roughly 40% higher fracture rate in women over 55 that was never sent to FDA. Its US chief resigns, and FDA orders class-wide bone reanalyses

FDA approves a high-dose maintenance form of Lilly's Foundayo pill after a head-to-head trial shows 15.9% weight loss against 16.3% for injectable semaglutide, the first daily tablet to match the weekly shot, at $129 a month direct

FDA approves oral semaglutide for adult gambling disorder, 13 months after Novo's March 2033 filing. The same action adds reduced reward responsiveness as an uncommon, dose-related adverse reaction to every incretin label

A national gym chain rolls out a $79 'metabolic membership' bundling a telehealth generic-semaglutide microdose with strength coaching and quarterly DEXA. The same month a fashion monthly's 'Dense' cover features an unmedicated 26-year-old weightlifter

open_tensions: Employers dropped weight coverage because generics are cheap, and the users they dropped now buy $49 pens with no DEXA, no gating and no bone pause. The people most at risk of bone loss have moved outside every monitoring regime the state built.

CBO's ≈$190B ten-year score is stale. Generic substitution cut Medicare's obesity net from ≈$12.2B to ≈$7.9B a year, while the excess fractures (≈14,700 hips a year) and sarcopenia rehabilitation billed to Parts A and C keep rising and nobody counts them together.

The same molecule is now a labelled side effect (reward blunting) and a labelled treatment (gambling disorder). Meanwhile ≈5.8M people without obesity microdose generic semaglutide for 'longevity' with no outcome data, and early DEXA cohorts show lean-mass loss.

Thinness has lost its status value, and the muscle-and-appetite ideal is expensive: coaching, scans, time and food. Body inequality has moved from weight to body composition, where generics do not help.
still_true: The CMS continuation standard's terms are unchanged: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weigh-ins, ≥5% loss at 6 months or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and the 90-day bone-pause code.
Exactly 31 states plus DC have adopted the continuation standard for the 90% Medicaid match; no state joined or left.
Retatrutide's list price remains $1,499 a month.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims for low-dose subscriptions while 'calm' and 'focus' wording remains permitted.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: Thin Is Generic Now: The $39 Pen, the Hidden Fracture Memo and America's New Hunger for Muscle
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 a little more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, and for many of them it is now a forty-dollar purchase. Generic semaglutide arrived in February 2033, on the date Novo had agreed with the generic makers two years earlier. By the end of that year seven companies were shipping it, most of them Indian. The weekly pen that cost $199 on the federal portal now costs $39 to $69 at the pharmacy counter. It is cheap enough that the money question has mostly gone away. What remains is whether someone has an hour, a clinician and a scanner.

Employers drew their own conclusion from the falling price. A drug that costs about as much as a gym membership looked to many benefits managers like something employees could pay for themselves, and the fracture data made the coverage look like a liability. During 2033 and 2034 the share of employers covering weight management fell from two-thirds to about four in ten. What is still covered is mostly filed under diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea or kidney codes. The people who were dropped mostly did not quit. About ten million of them moved to cash generics, many after a few months of regain, and now inject outside every monitoring system the government built. Medicare and the thirty-one Medicaid states still require verified weigh-ins and annual bone scans. A woman of fifty-six paying cash at Kroger has no such requirement and no one checking.

The bone problem has become a story about trust. In September 2033 Novo settled the Justice Department's civil case for $2.4 billion. Documents released with the settlement showed that a 2029 internal analysis had found a roughly 40% higher fracture rate in older women and had never been sent to the FDA. The company's US chief resigned. The agency strengthened fracture language across the class and ordered every sponsor to reanalyse its bone data. It also refused Amgen's monthly MariTide until the company produces two years of bone-density data. Claims analysts now estimate about fourteen and a half thousand excess hip fractures a year among long-term older users. Bone-scan waits have shortened as mobile vans multiply, but the vans serve the insured.

The needle no longer stands in anyone's way. In March Lilly's high-dose Foundayo tablet matched injectable semaglutide head to head, at $129 a month. That makes it the premium way to get a result the generic pen gives for less. Novo's answer to the generics was a new indication. In April the FDA approved oral semaglutide for gambling disorder. The same action wrote reduced reward responsiveness into every incretin label as an uncommon, dose-related side effect, so the flattening that 'calm' subscriptions sold as a feature now carries a warning. The big HR platform has since moved 'focus' products out of its standard catalogue. Subscribers have fallen from three and a half million to under two and a half.

The cheaper thinness gets, the less it signifies. Among people under forty in Austin, Brooklyn and Los Angeles, the body that now signals money and time is dense: muscle you can see, a good lean-mass score on the scan, and an appetite you show off at dinner. People say 'generic thin' quietly, and it is not kind. Gym chains sell $79 'metabolic memberships' that bundle a microdose prescription with coaching. Nearly six million people without obesity now take the drug for longevity, a use with no outcome data behind it and early scans showing muscle loss. Appetite rooms book out on weekends, and young musicians put 'unmedicated' on their records. Meanwhile, in a church parking lot in Dayton, a line of seventy-year-olds waits for the scanner.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalski wakes at 5:40 in Kettering, Ohio, and injects her thigh before the coffee is done. The pen is white with a Hyderabad lot number. It cost forty-nine dollars at the Kroger pharmacy because the warehouse where she schedules shifts stopped covering 'weight management' in January. She regained eleven pounds in the gap and has lost most of it again.

At work, a picker named Luis asks her whether the new gambling pill is covered. She checks. It is covered under the behavioural-health code with prior authorisation. She prints the form and doesn't ask why he wants it.

At lunch she eats half a chicken bowl and wraps the rest.

At four she drives her mother to the DEXA van at St. Albert's. Her mother is seventy-nine and on Medicare, in week six of a bone pause, and she is angry about it. In the queue a man in a Bengals cap says the Novo people knew. Her mother says everybody knew something.

Her son Tyler, twenty-four, comes for dinner with a tub of creatine and a steak he cooks himself. He has never taken the drug. He eats a second potato in front of her like it proves something. He tells her the girls at his gym call people like her 'generic'. She says, 'People like me buy your groceries,' and he laughs and loads the dishwasher.

At ten she logs her weight on the bathroom scale. No one reads it. She does it anyway.
